Satellites often include on-board propulsion. The way orbital mechanics work, if you want to raise or lower your orbital altitude, you increase or decrease your velocity. You don't burn your rocket straight away from the Earth; you burn in the direction of travel, either with or against.

By burning perpendicular to the direction of travel, a satellite can change its angle of inclination, which is the angle of the satellite's orbit compared to an equatorial orbit.

In regards to orientation, they use reaction wheels. These are a pair of spinning wheels oriented at right angles to each other. By altering the individual speeds of the wheels' rotations, the gyroscopic effect produces a force in one direction. No propellant is needed; the kinetic energy of the satellite's orientation is derived from the movement of the reaction wheels.
